routes.label: Check the six possible x values

question: Positive integers \(x\) and \(y\) satisfy the equation \(57x + 22y = 400.\) What is the least possible value of \(x + y?\)
solution:
Positivity makes \(x\) small, and parity cuts the possible values in half. Since \(y\ge1\),
\[
57x=400-22y\le378,
\]
so \(1\le x\le6\). Also, \(57x=400-22y\) is even. Because \(57\) is odd, \(x\) must be even. Thus \(x\) is \(2\), \(4\), or \(6\).

For each candidate, \(400-57x\) must equal \(22y\), so it must be divisible by \(22\).

| \(x\) | \(400-57x\) | Remainder upon division by \(22\) |
|---|---|---|
| \(2\) | \(286\) | \(0\) |
| \(4\) | \(172\) | \(18\) |
| \(6\) | \(58\) | \(14\) |

The remainders follow from \(286=22\cdot13\), \(172=22\cdot7+18\), and \(58=22\cdot2+14\). Only \(x=2\) works, giving \(y=13\).

There is therefore just one positive-integer solution, so the least possible sum is
\[
x+y=2+13=\boxed{15},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).

solutionMethods.explanation:
Taking remainders after division by \(22\) removes the term \(22y\). We write \(u\equiv v\pmod{22}\) when \(u-v\) is divisible by \(22\). The equation gives
\[
57x\equiv400\pmod{22},
\qquad 13x\equiv4\pmod{22}.
\]
To isolate \(x\), notice that
\[
13\cdot17=221=22\cdot10+1.
\]
Thus multiplying the congruence by \(17\) gives
\[
x\equiv68\equiv2\pmod{22}.
\]
In other words, \(x-2\) is a multiple of \(22\).

Since \(y\ge1\), we also have
\[
57x\le400-22=378,
\]
so \(1\le x\le6\). The only number in this range congruent to \(2\) modulo \(22\) is \(x=2\). Substitution yields
\[
y=\frac{400-57\cdot2}{22}=13.
\]
This is the unique positive-integer solution, so the least possible sum is \(\boxed{15}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
solutionMethods.label: Use remainders modulo 22
